items.label: 1A
items.claim: Yale's genome core still lists the NovaSeq 6000 next to the X Plus and AVITI on a page updated Apr 2026, so a top-tier academic core has not retired its 6000.
items.detail: The YCGA equipment page lists five sequencers: NovaSeq X Plus, NovaSeq 6000, MiSeq, Element AVITI and NextSeq 2000. It shows no retirement notice or counts, and the page is dated 10 Apr 2026. The 6000 and AVITI both sit alongside the X, so Yale is running a mixed fleet and the 6000 has not been replaced one-for-one.
items.source_name: Yale Center for Genome Analysis equipment page
items.why_new: Yale was not among the cores already checked (known list covers Northwestern, UCLA, TGen, MSU and others).

items.label: 1A
items.claim: UNMC's genomics core lists the NovaSeq 6000 (SP, S1, S2, S4) with AVITI24 and now Ultima, and shows no NovaSeq X.
items.detail: The services page (© 2026) lists AVITI24, the NovaSeq 6000 with SP/S1/S2/S4 flow cells, and says it 'now also' supports Ultima for selected projects. No X Plus is listed. The core is stacking two non-Illumina short-read platforms on top of a 6000-only Illumina base, so it is both a 6000 holdout and a place where rivals are being added.
items.quote: We now also support sequencing on the Ultima platform
items.why_new: Re-read of the page at 2026 date confirms Ultima has been added. Earlier notes had UNMC as 6000 plus AVITI24 only.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Wayne State's genome sciences core describes the NovaSeq 6000 as its latest platform and lists no X, AVITI or Ultima.
items.detail: The page calls the 6000 'the latest' platform the core has 'operationalized' and names no other sequencer. The page has no date, so it may be stale. If current, it is a pure 6000 holdout with no conversion plan visible.
items.why_new: Wayne State is not in the known core list.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: MD Anderson's Advanced Technology Genomics Core still cites its NovaSeq 6000 (NIH S10 award) while promoting the X Plus as a 'New Service'.
items.detail: The 2026 page keeps the NovaSeq 6000 acknowledgment (S10 1S10OD024977-01) and lists the NovaSeq X Plus as a new service. The core supports 225+ PIs and 243 grants. The 6000 is still in the fleet, with the X added alongside it rather than replacing it.
items.why_new: The known notes use only MDACC price ratios, not its fleet listing.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UMN Genomics Center lists AVITI24, NovaSeq X+, NextSeq 2000, MiSeq, Nanopore, Revio and Ultima UG 100, with no 6000.
items.detail: The page names the AVITI24 as newly installed. Illumina is down to the X+ and mid/low-throughput boxes. A research core with three non-Illumina or non-short-read additions and no 6000 shows research capacity being rebuilt around rivals. The known notes already hold UMN pricing, but not this fleet snapshot.
items.why_new: Gives the full fleet list; known notes cover UMN pricing and UMGC primarily.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: EMBL Genomics Core Facility's short-read fleet is NovaSeq X Plus plus Element AVITI24, with no 6000.
items.detail: The page (images uploaded Apr 2026) lists MiSeq i100, NextSeq 2000, NovaSeq X Plus and AVITI24, plus long-read systems. No 6000 and no Ultima. A major European research institute has paired AVITI24 with the X, adding a rival in 2025-26.
items.why_new: EMBL is not in the known core list.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Northwestern's NUSeq now lists only the X Plus, AVITI and Complete Genomics T1+ for short-read, a three-vendor fleet with no 6000.
items.detail: NUSeq's technology page lists NovaSeq X Plus, Element AVITI, DNBSEQ-T1+, NextSeq 500 and MiSeq. Search results note the X Plus has been offered since Sep 2023 and the DNBSEQ-G400 was added. The 6000 is not mentioned. Three vendors in one research core at mid-throughput shows broad rival entry.
items.why_new: Adds the T1+ addition to the known Northwestern pricing notes.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Of the cores whose pages loaded, most research cores no longer list a 6000, which cuts against a thick research 6000 tail.
items.detail: Count of 10 cores with readable fleet pages: 6000 listed at Yale, UNMC, Wayne State, MD Anderson (4 of 10, 40%). No 6000 at UMN, EMBL, NUSeq, plus Bonn and UMGC from earlier notes (6 of 10). Page fetches for Stanford, Princeton, Penn, Vanderbilt, HudsonAlpha, WashU and Baylor did not give fleet lists. This is a small, non-random sample.
items.why_new: First tally of 6000-retention across cores in this scrape.

notes: Employment pages gave little. Many big-core pages (Stanford SGTC, WashU GTAC, Vanderbilt VANTAGE, HudsonAlpha, Penn, Princeton, Baylor, Columbia, Broad, Mayo, CHOP) returned 403, certificate errors, connection refused or no fleet list; Michigan AGC returned 403.
